summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas transplant, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, chronic heart failure, and recent hospitalization for anemia and hypotension was readmitted for fatigue, weakness, and left leg swelling. She was found to have bilateral deep vein thromboses and was started on heparin. A stool test confirmed Clostridioides difficile infection, which was treated with oral vancomycin, leading to improvement in her fatigue and nausea. Her hemoglobin dropped transiently, requiring one unit of packed red blood cells, but remained stable thereafter. An MRI of the head showed no acute abnormalities, with findings consistent with chronic small vessel disease. Warfarin was restarted, and she was transitioned to extended care with plans for outpatient follow-up in nephrology, hematology, and primary care to manage ongoing anticoagulation, dialysis, and neurologic symptoms.
